label: Latent space and patches: from a million numbers to 256 tokens
context: Phase 1: a 256×256 colour image (draw a simple procedural picture: sky gradient, sun circle, hills) labelled 'image 3 × 256 × 256 = 196,608 numbers'. Phase 2: an autoencoder trapezoid 'VAE encoder' compresses it into a smaller 32×32 grid of 4-channel cells (draw as a smaller blurred-looking mosaic with 4 stacked layers), labelled 'latent 4 × 32 × 32 = 4,096 numbers (÷48)'. Phase 3: the latent is cut into 2×2 patches (grid lines appear), each patch flies out into a long row of tokens (show maybe 20 and an ellipsis), labelled '256 tokens'. Phase 4: caption 'the transformer works on tokens; the VAE decoder restores the pixels at the end' and the process reverses back to the image. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: From pixels to a latent grid to 256 tokens
spec.caption: A 256×256 colour image (196,608 numbers) is compressed by the VAE encoder into a 4×32×32 latent (4,096 numbers, ÷48). The latent is cut into 2×2 patches, and each patch becomes one of 256 tokens for the transformer. The VAE decoder then restores the pixels, so the process runs back to the image.
